biography: John Potter's racing journey began not on a pristine track, but on the dusty backroads of rural Oklahoma. As a kid, he spent countless hours tearing around in his grandfather's beat-up pickup, honing his reflexes and developing a raw, untamed driving style. His competitive spirit ignited during local dirt track races, where he quickly gained a reputation for fearless overtakes and relentless aggression. A pivotal moment came at age 19 when, against all odds, he won a regional championship, catching the attention of an AMR talent scout. Now at 27, Potter is a rising star in the AMR stable, proving his worth on the international stage. Though still relatively new to the world of professional racing, Potter shows that he's not afraid to make enemies along the way, and is willing to risk it all for a shot at victory.
drivingStyle: Potter's driving style is characterized by controlled aggression and a relentless pursuit of every tenth of a second. He's known for his late-braking maneuvers and willingness to divebomb into corners, often pushing the limits of adhesion. While his tire management can be inconsistent, especially under pressure, his raw speed and fearless attitude frequently allow him to overcome these shortcomings. He thrives in chaotic races, where his aggressive style can pay dividends, and he rarely backs down from a challenge, making him a formidable opponent in wheel-to-wheel combat.

rivalries.reason: A clash during a wet race at Spa, where Potter punted Alvarez off the track, led to a bitter feud that continues to this day.
Rossi publicly criticized Potter's aggressive driving style, calling him reckless and dangerous, sparking a war of words both on and off the track.
Potter and Tanaka had a heated battle for the lead at the Suzuka Circuit, culminating in a controversial overtake that cost Tanaka the race. Tanaka has accused Potter of unsportsmanlike conduct.

quirks: Always wears the same faded Oklahoma Sooners t-shirt under his racing suit.
Listens to a specific country song playlist before every race to calm his nerves.
Has a habit of tapping the steering wheel three times before the start of each lap.
famousQuote: "Second place is just the first loser. I'm here to win, no matter what it takes."
careerHighlight: Winning the 24 Hours of Le Mans in his debut year, driving the final stint and holding off a hard-charging veteran driver to secure the victory.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead on the final lap of the Daytona 500, costing him a potential championship victory and earning him the ire of his team.
